research.title: A Practical Causal Framework for Autonomous Mobile Robots: From Simulation to Real-World Human Environments
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Causal inference has emerged as a powerful paradigm enabling robots to make safe, efficient decisions by reasoning about the ``why'' behind events. However, its real-world application is hindered by the difficulty of collecting causal data, especially. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: CoReMatch: Recurrent Continuous Coordinate Refinement for Real-Time Robotic Feature Matching
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Feature matching underpins many robotic perception tasks, including visual localization, mapping, SLAM, and autonomous navigation. Existing semi-dense matchers predict confidence on fixed grids, limiting correspondences to predefined locations and requiring costly high-resolution grids for precise localization. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: From Roadside Sensing to Risk-Informed Safety Control: Surrogate Safety Measures as a Cyber-Physical Interface
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Proactive intersection safety analysis depends on trajectory data whose reliability varies by sensing modality, yet infrastructure-perception and surrogate safety measure (SSM) research have only recently begun to converge. This paper synthesizes both literatures alongside control theory. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: ISAC-Assisted Proactive Handover in mmWave Networks: Value of Foresight and Localization Requirements
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) links can lose tens of decibels within milliseconds when a person or vehicle crosses the line of sight, and reactive handover recovers only after the outage has begun. Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) promises. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: MABEL: An Open Anthropomorphic Mobile Bimanual Platform for Teleoperation and Learning
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: As robot learning moves beyond the tabletop, many tasks require mobility, adjustable reach, active perception, and bimanual dexterity. Commercial platforms combining these capabilities are costly, while affordable open-source alternatives cover only a subset and require software. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
